summary: A choice that stays selected, as one control: two to five short options on a track, with the current one on a raised thumb.

pairs.dont: Use a ButtonGroup with one button styled as selected.
pairs.do: Use a SegmentedControl when one option stays selected.
pairs.why: Nothing in a ButtonGroup stays pressed, so a faked selected state reads as two different buttons. The thumb on a track says one of these is the current value.

pairs.dont: Leave the control with nothing selected.
pairs.why: It is a radio group: once something is chosen there is no way back to nothing, and an empty track looks broken rather than unanswered.

pairs.dont: Put six options, or labels that need a sentence, on one track.
pairs.do: Keep it to two to five short labels. Beyond that, use Select or a RadioGroup.
pairs.why: Every option shares one row. Past five, or with long labels, the segments get too narrow to read or the control overflows on a phone.

pairs.dont: Use it to switch between panels of different content.
pairs.do: Use Tabs when each option shows a different panel.
pairs.why: A segmented control sets a value and is announced as a radio group. Tabs own a panel each and are announced as tabs. The two look alike and promise different things.

pairs.dont: Leave the control without a name.
pairs.do: Give it an aria-label, or a visible label beside it: "Order", "View".
pairs.why: "Ascending, radio, 1 of 2" does not say what is being ordered. The group's name supplies it.

a11y: role="radiogroup" with role="radio" items, so it is announced as one choice with a position: "Ascending, radio, 1 of 2".
One tab stop. Left and Right arrows move the selection, as in any radio group.
It needs a name: aria-label on the control, or aria-labelledby pointing at a visible label.
Selection is carried by the thumb and by the label's colour, not by colour alone.
